news.title: How Do the Latest Black Sea Attacks Affect Global Food Security?
news.summary_en: For the first time since 2022, attacks on agricultural infrastructure and cargo vessels are limiting grain exports from Russia and Ukraine at the same time. CSIS experts examine the latest attacks, their food-security impacts, and how the Iran war is worsening the crisis.

news.title: Hormuz Needs a Community, Not a Condominium
news.summary_en: A deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz that sidelines Gulf states would entrench coercion and invite a new conflict. Postwar Europe offers a better model: a shared governance mechanism that dilutes leverage and fosters long-term cooperation.

news.title: The Billion-Dollar Chip: Who Can Afford to Design the Future?
news.summary_en: As the cost of designing leading-edge chips approaches $1 billion, frontier semiconductor design is becoming accessible to fewer firms. The United States must reduce the underlying cost of design to preserve innovation and competitiveness across critical industries.

news.title: Imagining an Insurgency in Post-Revolutionary Iran
news.summary_en: What if the United States invades Iran to restore regional stability? Iran’s post-regime military strategy would rely on insurgent warfare to draw the United States into a protracted conflict, impeding U.S. efforts to achieve long-term political goals.

news.title: Does Vietnam’s Soaring U.S. Trade Deficit Make It a Bad Actor?
news.summary_en: There is little if any justification for any trade policy crackdown on Vietnam for allegedly being a bad actor, harming U.S. economic interests, or aiding and abetting China’s trade interests.

news.title: Adapting to the New Terrorism Landscape 25 Years After 9/11
news.summary_en: Post-9/11 counterterrorism efforts made large, foreign-directed attacks harder to execute. Stopping the terrorist threat that remains today requires a new approach.

news.title: Building Quantum-Ready Infrastructure: Preparing for the Physical Demands of Quantum Computing
news.summary_en: To avoid delays similar to the ones that the AI industry has experienced, the U.S. quantum industry needs to strengthen its supply chains for cryogenics, laser, optics, and other materials. Governments, firms, laboratories, and universities have a rare planning window.

news.title: Where’s the Beef This Time?
news.summary_en: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch examines the trade and non-trade causes of rising U.S. beef prices, as well as attempts by the White House and Department of Agriculture to limit the impact on the agriculture industry.

news.title: Educating the Kingdom at Home
news.summary_en: This installment of Charting the Middle East examines the kingdom's shift from financing overseas education to strengthening domestic educational capacity as part of its broader economic transformation.
